2609.39710.title: Drift Inspector: Exploring and Measuring Scientific Drift with Atomic Contribution Claims
2609.39710.paper_summary: Scientific abstracts mix contributions with background, motivation, and meta-language, so tools that read them as-is cannot separate what a field produces from what it discusses. We present Drift Inspector, an open-source system for measuring and exploring how a research field changes over time at the level of Atomic Contribution Claims (ACCs): decontextualized, contribution-bearing propositions an LLM extracts from each abstract before analysis. The system clusters these claims across years into an interactive map where every trend traces back to the claims and papers behind it. Applied to six years of EMNLP, it shows the field shifting away from classic NLP tasks toward LLM-era capabilities such as reasoning and multimodality -- a movement that keyword or whole-abstract counts blur. The released data extend beyond EMNLP: the same pipeline has processed the full ACL Anthology (346k claims, 80k abstracts, 423 venues). Extraction is human-validated and clustering checked against an external manually constructed taxonomy.
2609.39710.paper_summary_zh: 科學摘要將貢獻與背景、動機和元語言混合在一起，因此以原樣閱讀它們的工具無法分辨一個領域所產出的內容與其討論的內容。我們提出了 Drift Inspector，一個開源系統，用於測量和探索研究領域如何隨著時間變化，具體在原子貢獻聲明（Atomic Contribution Claims, ACCs）的層面上：這些是 LLM 從每個摘要中提取出的去上下文化、承載貢獻的命題，然後進行分析。該系統將這些聲明按年份聚類成一個互動地圖，地圖上每一個趨勢都可以追溯到其背後的聲明和論文。應用於六年的 EMNLP，它顯示該領域正在從經典 NLP 任務轉向 LLM 時代的能力，例如推理和多模態——這一變化是關鍵詞或整個摘要計數所模糊的。發布的數據超越了 EMNLP：相同的管道已處理完整的 ACL 文獻集（346k 聲明，80k 摘要，423 個會議）。提取經過人工驗證，聚類則是根據外部手動構建的分類法進行檢查。
